summary: AI observability tools help teams monitor, debug, and optimize LLM applications by tracking traces, token usage, latency, costs, and output quality in production. As LLM apps scale, these tools are essential for catching regressions, controlling spiraling API costs, and evaluating model performance against real-world usage. Choosing the right tool depends on whether your priority is cost tracking, deep tracing, experiment management, or ML-wide observability.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: LLM traces, chains, agent steps, token usage, latency, costs, and evaluation metrics across LLM application workflows.
features: Deep tracing of LangChain and non-LangChain apps
tools.pricing: Free Developer tier (1 seat, 5K traces/mo); Plus at $39/seat/mo; Enterprise with custom pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams building with LangChain or LangGraph who need tight integration between tracing, evaluation, and prompt iteration.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests, token usage, costs per model/user/session, latency, caching efficiency, and rate limits.
features: One-line proxy integration for cost and usage tracking
Request caching to cut redundant API calls
tools.pricing: Free tier (10K requests/mo); Pro at $20/seat/mo; Team and Enterprise tiers with higher limits and custom pricing.
tools.best_for: Developers who want fast, proxy-based cost monitoring and caching with minimal code changes.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
tools.monitors: End-to-end ML experiments, model training metrics, LLM traces (via W&B Weave), token usage, and evaluations.
features: W&B Weave for LLM app tracing and evaluation
tools.pricing: Free for personal use; Teams starting around $50/user/mo; Enterprise with custom pricing.
tools.best_for: ML teams needing unified observability across traditional model training and modern LLM application workflows.

tools.name: Arize AI
tools.monitors: Model performance, data drift, embedding drift, LLM traces, token usage, and quality/eval metrics in production.
features: Drift and data quality monitoring at scale
LLM tracing and evaluation via Arize Phoenix (open source)
Support for both ML and LLM observability
tools.pricing: Free open-source Phoenix; AX Free tier available; Pro and Enterprise tiers with custom pricing.
tools.best_for: Enterprises running ML and LLM systems at scale that need rigorous drift detection and RAG debugging.

tools.name: LangFuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, nested spans, token usage, costs, latency, prompt versions, and evaluation scores.
features: Evaluation framework with LLM-as-judge and human scoring
Detailed cost and token analytics per trace
tools.pricing: Free self-hosted (open source); Cloud Hobby free tier; Core at $29/mo; Pro and Enterprise tiers available.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting an open-source, self-hostable observability stack with full data control and flexible integrations.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM calls, token usage, latency, and traces using OpenTelemetry standards, exportable to any OTel-compatible backend.
features: Auto-instrumentation for popular LLM SDKs and frameworks
Exports to Datadog, Grafana, Honeycomb, and more
tools.pricing: Free open-source SDK; Traceloop hosted platform offers free tier plus paid plans with custom pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams with existing observability infrastructure who want standards-based LLM telemetry without lock-in.

cost_tips: Cache repeated or similar requests so identical prompts don't trigger redundant paid API calls, and enable provider-side prompt caching where supported.
Route tasks to the cheapest capable model—use smaller or distilled models for simple tasks and reserve frontier models for complex reasoning.
Minimize token usage by trimming prompts, truncating context, summarizing long histories, and setting sensible max_tokens limits on outputs.
Set per-user and per-key rate limits plus budget alerts, and batch requests where possible to reduce overhead and catch runaway spending early.
